title: 칭찬을 들었을 때: 잘하기는요, 아직 멀었어요
objective: By the end, you can reply to a compliment or a light remark with -기는요 / -긴요 (polite) or -기는 / -긴 (casual), and add what is really true.
summary: Learn to answer a compliment politely and modestly with -기는요 (-긴요, -기는, -긴), like saying "Oh, not really."

task.title: Reply to compliments modestly
task.line: Read each situation, then choose, fill in, fix, or write a modest reply with -기는(요).

forms.when: Polite reply to someone you say -요 to (coworkers, teachers, older people).
forms.means: Oh, not really. / Not at all. (modest denial)
forms.example: A: 한국어를 정말 잘하시네요. B: 잘하기는요. 아직 많이 틀려요.
forms.exampleMeaning: A: Your Korean is really good. B: Oh, not really. I still make lots of mistakes.

forms.when: Same politeness as -기는요; very common in speech.
forms.example: A: 요리 솜씨가 대단하네요. B: 대단하긴요. 인터넷 보고 따라 했어요.
forms.exampleMeaning: A: You're an amazing cook. B: Not at all. I just copied a recipe online.

forms.when: Casual. Only with close friends or younger people you speak 반말 to.
forms.example: A: 그 가방 진짜 예쁘다. B: 예쁘긴. 그냥 싼 거야.
forms.exampleMeaning: A: That bag is really pretty. B: Nah. It's just a cheap one.

forms.form: Adjective stem + 기는요 (light denial, not a compliment)
forms.when: When someone guesses something about you and you gently say it is not so, to be modest or to not worry them.
forms.example: A: 요즘 많이 바쁘시죠? B: 바쁘기는요. 괜찮아요.
forms.exampleMeaning: A: You must be very busy these days. B: Not really. I'm fine.

watchOut: 끝냈기는요 (X) → 끝내기는요 (O): Use the plain stem, even when you talk about the past. Then say the real situation: 끝내기는요. 아직 반도 못 했어요.
To your teacher: 예쁘긴. (X) → 예쁘기는요. (O): Without 요, it is casual and sounds rude to people you should speak politely to.
잘 치기는 해요 (X for 'not really') → 잘 치기는요 (O): -기는 해요 means 'I do, but…'. It agrees with the compliment. Only -기는요 says 'not really'.
exercises: Choose the right reply for each person: ① (your close friend) 너 요즘 날씬해졌다! — (날씬하긴 / 날씬하긴요). 요즘 많이 먹어. ② (your team leader) 민수 씨는 정말 부지런하네요. — (부지런하긴 / 부지런하기는요). 저도 가끔 늦어요.
Fill in the blank with -기는요 to reply modestly: A: 집이 정말 깨끗하네요. B: ____. 어제 급하게 치웠어요.
Find the mistake and write the correct word: A: 숙제 벌써 다 했어요? B: 했기는요. 아직 시작도 못 했어요.
Choose the reply that politely says 'Oh, not really': A: 한국 음식을 잘 만드시네요. ⓐ 잘 만들기는요. 아직 배우는 중이에요. ⓑ 잘 만들기는 해요. 매일 하니까요.
Answer in Korean with -기는요, then add one sentence about the real situation: A: 영어 발음이 정말 좋네요. B: ____.
answers: 좋기는요. 아직 연습을 많이 해야 해요. (좋긴요. + any sentence about the real situation)
